The key sits on the blotter. Brass, small teeth, no hotel tag. Machine oil and river.
File the night. The key stays on the blotter.
Work the morning. If the gray overcoat comes looking for the key, he can take a number.
Come in out of the wet. Tell me what you know.
Sit down. Tuesday night: last place, last call, last person who saw her.
Convince me she didn't take a taxi and a room.
My sister Lillian vanished Tuesday night. Not went away. The apartment lights were still on. The kettle was still warm.
Mr. Voss? Forgive the hour. They told me to wait until morning.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.key.revea: Since I found it, a man has been following me. Gray overcoat. Black gloves. He waits across from my boarding house and turns away when I look. He doesn't wave.
Sewn into the lining was a brass key. Small. Old teeth. No hotel tag. Lillian still sews her own hems. She would not leave a coat that cost her a week.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.b.te: If the gray overcoat comes looking for the key, don't give it to him. I hired you to find my sister.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.text: Please find her, Mr. Voss. Find the sister—not the coat's alibi.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.police.st: I asked for the night sergeant's notes. He offered coffee and a speech about tides. I asked who benefited if Lillian stopped reading manifests. He stopped offering coffee.
Harborpoint PD filed it soft: missing adult, no signs of struggle, coat recovered, probable drowning, case cooling before the ink dried. They were polite. They did not offer the file.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.cyn: Lillian hated the river. She hated unfinished books more. The police found her coat and called it an answer. I put my hands in the lining.
If she had a taxi receipt I would not be here.
Fine. Bill your hours. Look at the coat first. Whoever emptied it left the key.
At least you're honest about the bill.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait by the phone.
You'll take it. That's enough. You get the key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.goo: Lillian worked late at the shipping office near Wharf Ladder—ledgers, manifests. She never missed a tram. Tuesday she left work at nine. By midnight the river had her coat.
Thank you. I can pay thirty now. The rest when you find her.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait by the phone.
The follower: tall, hat brim low, gloves that stay on. He never crosses the street. He only makes sure I know it's his.
I'll take the promise. I'll walk carefully.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.neu: Last confirmed: Wharf Ladder shipping office, Tuesday, nine o'clock. She told a clerk she had one more errand uptown. No name. No cab from the desk phone. Midnight, river watch found her coat on the stones below the old iron stairs—empty. Arranged.
They handed the coat back in a paper bag. I took it home and found the key they did not feel for.
That's the work I came to buy. The river stones, the duty roster, the shipping office clock that runs three minutes fast when the night crew wants an alibi.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait by the phone.
I'll stay with a friend on Printers' Quarter tonight. Real locks. Fewer witnesses who owe the docks a favor.
Gray overcoat, black gloves, no limp, no badge. Bakery doorway across from my stairs, eleven to one. When a streetcar passes, he uses the noise to move. Professional habits.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.pre: I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait by the phone.
Fine. Lillian was reading manifests. I don't have the names clean enough for a courtroom. I have a sister and a key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.key: Describe the follower once more, then go somewhere with a real lock.
If anyone asks, I never saw a key.
Tell me what you're still not saying. What did Lillian find in those manifests?

I'm leaving the key if you'll take the case. I can pay thirty now. The rest when you find her.

Tell me how you want to play this.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.pol: I pull the file they won't show you.
The drowning's too tidy. I'll hear how they said it.
I'll tell the sergeant I believe him. See who relaxes.
The police have a coat. I have a sister. What do you do with that?
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.voss.monologue: Rain had been at the glass since afternoon. I had not.
Three unpaid notices. Same name on all of them.
Radiator ticks. Pipes in the walls. Rain on the glass. Same as yesterday.

I told myself I was done with missing persons. The rent said otherwise.

Then the hallway. Heels on tired boards. A pause outside the door.

A woman out of the rain. A coat with no body in it.

The door opened.
Three old cases, two unpaid bills, one clean page.
The hall smelled worse, but at least it led somewhere.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.files.node.inspection: Closed, abandoned, and one I still lied about.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.phone.node.inspection: Quiet. For once it had the decency to look guilty.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.window.node.inspectio: Same rain, same glass. Now I had a client.
The rain had been at the glass longer than I had.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.client-retained: Retained by Lila March. The Empty Coat is open.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.pressed-hard: Pushed Lila on what the police finished too early. Manifests.
